newsitem.title: UK: World oil price soars as cold weather sets in.
newsitem.headline: World oil price soars as cold weather sets in.

text.p: World oil prices soared on Thursday as the year's first cold spell hit the United States and rekindled market fears that heating oil stocks in the world's biggest energy-consuming country were too low to meet demand.
November futures for benchmark Brent Blend crude gained 64 cents to close at $23.71 a barrel. But crude oil was outpaced by gas oil, which is used for domestic heating.

October gas oil on London's International Petroleum Exchange ((IPE) closed $3.50 a tonne up on Thursday, making a total gain of more than $10 in the last two days as it tracked U.S. heating oil futures on the New York market.
U.S. heating oil inventories at the end of last week were roughly one third below last year's levels, according to Energy Information Administration data released on Wednesday.

The first cooler autumn temperatures sweeping across the U.S. Northeast, where heating oil consumption is highest, and colder weather in the U.S. Midwest pushed heating oil on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) set a new contract high.
"People are looking at the low stock situation and are severely worried about what will happen when winter hits," a broker said.
Both European gas oil, which includes heating oil, and U.S. heating fuels, were trading at their highest levels in five years after a strong rally which began on Wednesday.

U.S. refineries have been pushing production to the limit in order to raise heating oil inventories but traders have in recent weeks been shipping some of the oil across to Europe, where stocks are also low and prices higher.

"Heating oil is being sold into Europe and the U.S. is not building any inventories. Some American traders are looking short term and making fast bucks," said Charles Gray, first vice-president at Prudential-Bache Futures Ltd in London.

Traders said the apparent failure of the Washington talks to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli dispute had no immediate impact on oil prices although the market was watching the region with interest for any sign of an escalating crisis.

"It is a one-way street at the moment. A lot of people are standing on the sidelines afraid to sell and if gas oil is given a further boost by U.S. heating oil, the fear now is that we will get a cold winter and possible more violence in the Middle East," Gray said.
Crude oil prices in dollars per barrel.
